I started playing trumpet at 8 years old. My grandfather gave my his King Liberty Model that he played all through college. He paid for his tuition by playing in jazz bands and, after seeing all the pictures of him jamming when he was young and having that horn handed down to me, I knew I wanted to be a professional musician.

I actively played trumpet until I was about 20, picking up trombone, baritone, guitar, and a little piano along the way. My senior year in high school, I was really into punk and hardcore music and decided I wanted to start a band. I wanted to be the vocalist. I found other musicians and started writing and playing as much music as I possibly could. Then we recorded an EP, printed some shirts, and started playing local shows. Then we started selling out local shows. Then we started touring regionally and selling out shows all up and down the west coast. It was fucking great! My dream come true! We were consistency profiting off of tours, getting monthly payments from iTunes, and getting over 10,000 plays per day on MySpace.

This is where it takes a turn....

We signed a record deal, signed with a management group, and signed with a booking agent. All the sudden, we we're going on tours that had better turnouts, selling more merch, and getting more downloads online than ever before, yet, we were coming home from tour >$1000 in the hole. 15% of gross admission and merch sales to management, 15% to booking, 15% to the label. Not to mention we signed a "standard indie deal," according to our lawyer, that split royalties 85/15% in favor of the label for any music we sold online.

We kept an insane tour schedule of 2 months on/ 2 weeks off. All-in-all we were on the road 8-9 months per year. Barely able to eat, losing money, getting angry at eachother due to the stress. It was horrible.

We finally broke up. Ended up >$20,000 in debt which I'm still paying off today.

All I wish, looking back, is that I never gave up trumpet for the chance at becoming "big."

I was top of the class in primary school. Totally loved learning everything (still do) and had no problem with authority what so ever. Moved on to high school where I was topping the year in math and constantly being egged on to join debating teams and the such as I was doing well at English and loved reading (still do)... then one ill-fated evening I won a Sex Pistols album when I phoned into a radio station. I had never really heard of them much and I certainly had no real idea how massively they had impacted the world in general. So I gave it a spin and my world turned upside down. Next thing I was chasing down Dead Kennedy's records, shaving my hair into giant fluorescent mohawks, dressing like a maniac and totally sticking it to the man via playing in punk bands and disregarding anything my teachers told me... oh to be young and impressionable. Twenty years later and I'm still a punk rocker at heart and sitting hear with a guitar in my hands. That Sex Pistols record REALLY opened my eyes!

It has a very great impact on my view of the world. When I was 11, I "experimented" with my music taste. What I did is listening to rock, punk, etc. I found out that the underground music genres aren't that offensive and awful as I once thought. Because of this, I have a wide music taste.

But why does it change my view of the world? Because it taught me that what others doesn't like, may be likeable to you. That sort of motivated me to experiment more and more things and thus I have a wide view. Before I was 11, I was a bit religious and I always hear "Liberal is bad and religion is good, atheism is horrible". After a bit experimentation, I see that the ideal wasn't always right. It's wrong to some, it's right to some.

After that I became an atheist and I became liberal. It made me the person I am today. It made me explore my sexuality and I found out that apparently I am a bisexual. If I found this out I would panic because of religion. So yeah, my music experimentation sort of made a very large impact on my life.

Also, I can express my emotions into the music. If I'm happy, I'll listen to Style, or if I'm a bit down I'll listen to Say Something, or maybe if I am angry I'll listen to Aimless Arrow, or if I want some peace I'll listen to Miserere Mei Deus.

So to recap, music made a very large impact on my life. It was so significant that me before experimenting with my music tastes and me after experimenting with my music tastes are almost two completely different people.
